FireTunnel is a VPN client for the TrustTunnel protocol. It encrypts your phone\'s traffic and sends it through your server. To connect you need a config: a link from your dashboard, a QR code, a file or details from the server administrator.

1. Open the Configs tab and tap Add. 2. Pick a way: By link — paste the link from your dashboard; QR code — scan it with the camera. You can also build a config in the constructor, paste TOML manually or open a .toml/.conf file. 3. Go back to the VPN tab and tap the big button. On the first connection Android asks you to allow the VPN — accept.

The big button turns the VPN on and off. Its shape shows the state: off, connecting (the button spins), connected (green). Tapping it while connecting cancels.
Above the button: the status and session time. Below: the active server with its ping, apps that skip the VPN, a speed chart for the last minute and session totals: received, sent and connections (via VPN / direct).
If connecting fails, the status turns red and shows the reason.

Tap the server card on the main screen to choose another config. Each shows its ping — the time to open a connection to the server: green is fast, amber is slow, “no response” means the server is unreachable.
Ping is measured outside the VPN, so it shows the real latency to the server. It refreshes every 30 seconds; tap the ping label to measure now.
If you switch servers while connected, the new one is used after reconnecting.

A link like firetunnel://enroll?url=… or https://…/enroll/… connects this device to your account. Open it from a browser, paste it or scan it as a QR code.
A config from such a link updates itself: on every app start, before connecting and in the background every 30 minutes. If the administrator changes the server details, the phone picks them up on its own.
If the device was removed in the dashboard or access was revoked, the config is deleted, the VPN disconnects and you get a notification. If the server is temporarily unavailable, the old config keeps working.

Use the constructor when the administrator gave you a server address, username and password rather than a ready file.
• Server address: vpn.example.com or vpn.example.com:8443 (port 443 by default). • Protocol: HTTP/2 works anywhere; HTTP/3 is faster on mobile networks but blocked on some. • DNS: AdGuard DNS without filtering by default; Cloudflare, Google or your own servers (tls:// and https:// too). • Advanced: backup addresses, TLS server name (SNI), anti-DPI, post-quantum encryption and skipping certificate verification — the last one is dangerous, for test servers only.

To make sure traffic never goes around the VPN, turn this on in Android: Settings → Connection → Always-on VPN and kill switch. In the system settings pick FireTunnel and turn on Always-on VPN and Block connections without VPN.
The VPN then starts by itself after a reboot, and apps cannot go online directly if the connection drops.

While the VPN is on, a notification shows the server and traffic; you can disconnect from it.
On Android 16 and newer it can appear in the status bar as a Live Update with the session timer. The switch is in Settings → Notifications. The system decides whether to show it; you can turn it off in Android\'s notification settings.

Once a day the app checks GitHub for a new version and offers to update; turn this off in Settings → Updates, where there is also a Check now button.
The downloaded file is verified (checksum and package name) before installing. Android asks you to let FireTunnel install apps — once.
Debug builds can only be updated after uninstalling them: they are signed with a different key.

Settings → Diagnostics → Logs shows the VPN core\'s connection log. Use Copy to send it to the developer.
Core log level sets the detail: As in the config, normal (info), detailed (debug) or everything (trace). Detailed levels are for troubleshooting only — they slow things down.

• The dashboard link is a secret: with it someone could connect their own device. It is stored encrypted and never written to the log. If it leaks, reissue it in the dashboard. • Config passwords are stored only on this device. • Enrolling sends only a device fingerprint (a hash, not the identifier itself) and the device name. • The app list is only used to pick apps outside the VPN and is never sent anywhere.
